headline.title: The latest AI news we announced in May 2026
headline.summary: In May 2026, several advancements in AI technology were announced, highlighting improvements in natural language processing and machine learning algorithms. Key developments included new models that enhance conversational AI capabilities and increased efficiency in data processing tasks.

articles.title: Startup Battlefield 200 applications officially close in 3 days
articles.summary: Applications for the Startup Battlefield 200 will close on June 8 at 11:59 p.m. PT, offering startups the opportunity to compete on the Disrupt Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their entries before the deadline.

articles.title: Google will pay SpaceX $920M per month for compute
articles.summary: Google has entered into a deal to pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing services, as announced on Friday. This agreement comes just a week before SpaceX's anticipated IPO.

articles.title: The ‘together tech’ wave might be the most intriguing startup bet of 2026
articles.summary: In 2026, some startups are focusing on fostering in-person connections and social experiences, diverging from the AI-centric fundraising trend. Notable examples include Brynn Putnam's Board, which emphasizes games and social interactions, and the viral Cyberdeck creators promoting DIY computers that encourage outdoor engagement.

articles.title: This is your laptop… on AI
articles.summary: During recent developer conferences, Big Tech leaders, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, emphasized the transformative potential of AI in everyday technology, particularly in how laptops are utilized. Huang outlined innovative approaches that could redefine user interaction and functionality in computing devices.

articles.title: AirTrunk commits $30B to build 5GW of AI data centers in India
articles.summary: AirTrunk has announced a $30 billion investment to establish 5GW of AI data center capacity in India. This initiative aims to enhance the country's infrastructure for data processing and storage.

articles.title: New York lawmakers pass one-year ban on new data centers
articles.summary: New York State lawmakers have approved a one-year moratorium on new large data centers, pending Governor Kathy Hochul's signature. The ban aims to allow time for policymakers to assess the environmental and energy price implications of such facilities.

articles.title: The token bill comes due: Inside the industry scramble to manage AI’s runaway costs
articles.summary: The AI industry is facing escalating costs, prompting a shift in focus from rapid expansion to implementing necessary safeguards and cost management strategies. Companies are now prioritizing the establishment of guardrails to control expenses associated with AI development and deployment.

articles.title: Has Microsoft Lost Its Mojo (Again)?
articles.summary: Microsoft's AI products are reportedly underperforming in sales, and GitHub is facing ongoing challenges. In an interview, VP Scott Hanselman discussed the company's current position and whether it is in a state of catch-up in the AI landscape.

articles.title: The Meta hack shows there’s more to AI security than Mythos
articles.summary: Attackers exploited Meta's AI customer support agent to steal Instagram accounts by requesting the linking of accounts to their own email addresses. This incident highlights vulnerabilities in AI security, as one attacker even gained access to a dormant Obama White House account.

articles.title: The most interesting startups right now want to get you off your phone
articles.summary: Startups like Board, founded by Brynn Putnam, are focusing on in-person social experiences and games, raising funds to encourage people to disconnect from their phones. Additionally, creators of Cyberdeck are gaining popularity by designing whimsical DIY computers that promote outdoor engagement.

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic May Be Rivals, but Investors Aren’t Picking Sides
articles.summary: Investors are showing interest in both OpenAI and Anthropic, viewing them as complementary players in the AI space rather than direct competitors. This perspective allows for diversified investment in the rapidly evolving AI industry.
